newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Governor begins packing as HK handover looms-paper.
newsitem.headline: Governor begins packing as HK handover looms-paper.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten and his wife Lavender have begun packing up two weeks before Britain's colonial rule in the territory comes to an end, a local newspaper said on Sunday.

The Pattens spent last week boxing up their clothes, household goods, souvenirs and gifts at their official residence on the slopes of Hong Kong Island, the South China Morning Post's Sunday edition said.
Hong Kong, a British colony for 156 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.

The couple will leave Government House for the last time in the afternoon of June 30 and will bid farewell to the territory of 6.4 million from the deck of royal yacht Britannia shortly after midnight.
The newspaper said some of their possessions were bound for France, the rest for England.
Patten, governor since 1992, has said he would spend some time in France, where the couple have a house, to write a book.
Officials from Government House were not immediately available for comments.
